recent_posts.title: Jason Fried on building sustainable software businesses and staying lean
recent_posts.summary: Jason Fried discusses his philosophy on building sustainable software businesses in a 2.5-hour podcast interview. Topics include building products for yourself, keeping costs low with small teams, fighting software bloat, prioritizing "enough" over growth, staying close to customers, working in six-week cycles, and maintaining independence through profitability. The conversation covers 37signals' approach to lean operations, intuition-driven product development, and defining success through pride in work rather than scale.

recent_posts.title: Great design was a Cuisinart
recent_posts.summary: The original Cuisinart food processor exemplifies excellent interface design through its simple two-button system: an ON button that latches for continuous operation, and a PULSE/OFF button that springs back when released. The large paddle buttons provide clear affordances, work with any hand condition, and demonstrate how physical interface design can be intuitive and functional through thoughtful mechanical behavior and generous surface area.

recent_posts.title: The joy of delegating to competence
recent_posts.summary: AI agents are exciting not just because of their technical capabilities, but because they democratize the experience of delegating to total competency. Previously, only managers of great teams knew the joy of trusting someone to complete tasks perfectly without oversight. Now, AI makes this level of reliable delegation accessible to everyone, creating genuine leverage and explaining the widespread enthusiasm for AI workflows.

recent_posts.title: Smart home technology makes basic tasks unnecessarily complex
recent_posts.summary: Modern smart home technology has made basic tasks unnecessarily complex. A new construction house equipped with IoT devices, touchscreen controls, and connected appliances creates frustrating user experiences compared to traditional physical interfaces. Light switches require demos, dishwashers need apps to operate, thermostats present confusing options, and everything suffers from lag. Physical switches, buttons with tactile feedback, and simple analog controls prove more intuitive and reliable than their "smart" counterparts. The contrast highlights how technology hasn't solved usability—it's regressed it.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Fizzy, our newest product
recent_posts.summary: Fizzy is a new open-source kanban board tool designed to simplify issue and idea tracking. It offers a clean, fast interface as an alternative to bloated tools like Trello, Jira, and Asana. The product provides 1000 free cards, with unlimited cards and users available for $20/month. Users can also self-host the open-source version for free and contribute to its development through pull requests.

recent_posts.title: Why beta testing should happen right before launch
recent_posts.summary: Beta testing works best when done late in development, just a week or two before launch at version 0.99. The goal isn't gathering fundamental feedback but using external users as a forcing function to clean up loose ends and polish details you've been postponing. Like preparing your house for dinner guests, knowing others will see your product motivates you to address those small issues you could live with internally but shouldn't ship publicly.

recent_posts.title: Simplicity wins when product categories become too complex
recent_posts.summary: Products don't need revolutionary features to succeed. When entire categories become bloated with complexity through competitive one-upmanship, opportunities emerge for simpler alternatives. Success comes from building grounded products that feel right and address what competitors overlooked, not from matching their feature sets.

recent_posts.title: When design drives behavior
recent_posts.summary: Explores how thoughtful design details can influence user behavior through the example of a luxury watch's power reserve indicator. The A. Lange & Söhne Lange 1 uses non-linear spacing and accelerated visual progression to make the power reserve appear to deplete faster than it actually does, encouraging owners to wind the watch more frequently and preventing it from stopping unexpectedly. This demonstrates how small interface design choices can materially change how users interact with products.

recent_posts.title: Preserve wealth instead of chasing returns after business exit
recent_posts.summary: A successful entrepreneur advises a young founder who recently sold his business for $2M to prioritize capital preservation over aggressive investment or reinvestment. The key recommendation is to keep the money safe in low-risk accounts rather than pursuing high-return opportunities, emphasizing that maintaining wealth is more important than growing it aggressively at a young age.

recent_posts.title: Marketing is transferring enthusiasm for what you build
recent_posts.summary: Marketing at its core is about transferring genuine enthusiasm for what you're building. When you're truly passionate about your vision and creating something you need, that authentic energy becomes your brand through action, not just messaging. Poor marketing transfers insecurities and false promises instead. Since everything communicates something, marketing is unavoidable and always reflects your true intentions, whether positive or negative.
